subject: POC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: POC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short PoC underway that answers your core question: which deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) best fits Acme’s performance, security, and budget requirements.

Summary from our discovery:
- Primary goal: integrate LLM into Customer Support triage for 2 product lines (Support A and Support B).
- KPIs: p95 inference latency <= 300ms for single-turn generation at 512 tokens; sustain 120 req/s for peak batch; end-to-end quality (F1 on triage labels) >= 88% vs current baseline.
- Data: only non-PII customer support transcripts will be used in the PoC; sensitive PII paths are blocked by Acme.
- Security needs: SOC2 evidence, VPC option desirable for Prod; Dedicated capacity preferred for predictable throughput.
- Timeline: target evaluation in April, decision by end of April.

Proposed PoC / trial plan (attached as acme-poc-trial-plan-20260320.pdf):
1) Scope (2 weeks): Prod-like load test + quality eval on a 2-week historical dataset for Support A.
2) Success criteria:
   - Performance: p95 token latency <= 300ms (hosted or dedicated measurement)
   - Throughput: sustain 120 req/s with <=10% error rate
   - Quality: F1 >= 88% on triage labels vs labeled sample
   - Security & compliance: SOC2 checklist + CNTRL access audit logs available
3) Deployment modes to test:
   - Hosted API (fastest to start)
   - Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — preferred by Acme for predictability
   - Private VPC pilot if SOC/legal requires network isolation (additional setup time)
4) Stakeholders: Samir (PM, Acme), Priya (Eng lead), Marissa (AE), Camila (SE). Rafael (AE Manager) will support approvals/credits.
5) Next steps:
   - Confirm scope & stakeholders by EOD Friday 3/20
   - Quick kickoff call — 30 min — propose Tues 3/24 or Wed 3/25
   - Redwood to provision an evaluation environment and share test harness + instructions

Attachments: acme-poc-trial-plan-20260320.pdf; also included a one-pager on deployment options (redwood-deployment-options-onepager.pdf).

Let me know any adjustments to objectives or timeline. If this looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop Rafael and Camila for SE support.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. A few quick notes and q's: 

- We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity for the PoC because predictability matters for our SLOs; we still want to understand the overhead to move to Private VPC if Prod requires it.
- Success criteria look right; can you confirm how you measure p95 latency (end-to-end vs token-only)? We want end-to-end including network and SDK overhead.
- Timeline: April evaluation and decision end of April sounds good. Can we do a 2-week PoC starting 4/6? Priya prefers early April for her team’s availability.
- Stakeholders: I'll add our infra lead (Tom Ellis) if we get to VPC validation — he’ll need to be on the security checklist.

Availability for kickoff: Tue 3/24 at 11 AM PT works for me.

Appreciate the one-pager; can the PoC include an estimate for expected token cost at your suggested batching/quantization settings?

Thanks,
Samir
Product Manager | Acme Corp
samir.gupta@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@acme.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-21T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial plan & deployment mode - Acme Corp

Samir — great, thanks for the quick reply and clarifications. Answers and updated plan below.

Latency measurement: we’ll report both token-level and end-to-end (SDK + network + runtime) p95. For the PoC we’ll use your prod-like test harness to measure E2E under an internal agent that mimics your client-side SDK.

Cost estimate: attached in the PoC plan — rough estimate for the 2-week PoC at expected load (~120 req/s peak, avg 75 req/s) using our recommended batching and fp16 quantized model is ~$7k in usage credits. We’ll provide exact numbers in the kickoff so you can see how batching and cache settings affect unit costs.

Updated PoC timeline (proposed):
- Week of 4/6: Provision environment (Hosted + Dedicated mirror) and run smoke tests
- Week of 4/13: Full 2-week load/quality run for Support A dataset (we can run Support B optionally if you want parallel runs)
- Week of 4/27: Evaluation & decision; Redwood to run a joint review and deliver results + recommendation

Success criteria (finalized):
- p95 E2E latency <= 300ms for single-turn at 512 tokens
- Sustained throughput >= 120 req/s with error rate <= 10%
- Quality F1 >= 88%
- SOC2 checklist items: access logs, audit trail, encryption at rest, KMS integration (for Dedicated/VPC)

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Acme: Samir (PM, product acceptance), Priya (eng lead, test harness), Tom Ellis (infra — VPC/security)
- Redwood: Marissa (AE, project lead), Camila (SE — PoC execution & tuning), Rafael (approvals/credits)

Next actions I’ll take:
1) Schedule kickoff for Tue 3/24 11 AM PT (proposed) — will send calendar invite
2) Provision evaluation environments and share test harness + runbook by 4/6
3) Share cost estimate and recommended batching/quant settings in the kickoff deck

I’m looping Camila here to confirm SE availability and to prepare the runbook. Camila — can you join the kickoff and own the provisioning/runbook?

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa
